quotes.quote: The main bundle of the fornix or postcommissural fornix finally traverses the hypothalamus, where most of its fibres terminate in the mamillary body.
The fornix is a large, compact, arch-shaped bundle that originates from the hippocampal formation and projects to the septal region and hypothalamus.
The mamillothalamic tract, which passes to the anterior thalamic nucleus, forms part of the so-called Papez circuit.

The fasciculus mamillaris princeps, containing the efferents of the mamillary nuclei, constitutes a large compact bundle that passes dorsally for a short distance and then splits into two components, the large mamillothalamic and smaller mamillotegmental
The anterior nuclear group receives the mamillothalamic tract.
The anterior and lateral dorsal nuclei are reciprocally connected with the limbic cortex of the cingulate gyrus, retrosplenial area and pre- and parasubiculum
The fibres originating from the anterior nuclei reach the temporal lobe via the cingulum and terminate in the subicular complex and, more specifically, in the presubiculum
This projection forms part of the so-called circuit of Papez, which will be discussed below.
The cingulum consists of a bundle of short and long association fibres that surround the corpus callosum.
Passing through the core of the cingulate and parahippocampal gyri, it extends from the septal area to the uncal region in the temporal lobe
The fibres passing from the entorhinal cortex to the dentate gyrus form a large pathway known as the temporo-ammonic or perforant path
They originate principally from large stellate cells situated in layer II of the entorhinal cortex and perforate through the subiculum and the zone of the obliterated hippocampal fissure.
After entering the dentate gyrus, these fibres ramify in the outer two thirds of the molecular layer of that structure, where they form excitatory synapses onto the dendritic spines of granule cells
The axons of the granule cells in the dentate gyrus pass as mossy fibres to the stratum radiatum of field CA3, in which they form a separate sublayer known as the stratum lucidum .
The mossy fibre varicosities contain large amounts of Zn 2+ and opioid peptides that are coreleased with the primary neurotransmitter glutamate
These collaterals are collectively known as Schaffer collaterals .
Physiological experiments have shown that the Schaffer collaterals exert an excitatory action on CA1 pyramidal cells
The CA1 pyramidal cells project massively to the subiculum
All of these projections originate from pyramidal neurons and are considered to be excitatory in nature.

Two cell masses, the laterodorsal tegmental (LDT) and pedunculopontine tegmental (PPT) nuclei, both situated in the tegmentum of the caudal midbrain and rostral pons.
These nuclei contain numerous neurons that use acetylcholine as a neurotransmitter.
The dorsal branch, which includes numerous cholinergic fibres from the LDT and PPT, passes to the thalamus itself and the reticular thalamic nucleus

Fibres ascending from the mesopontine cholinergic (LDT, PPT), noradrenergic (LC), and serotoninergic (DR, CS) cell groups and from other parts of the reticular formation together form an ascending arousal system (AAS).

The VLPO sends descending projections to the various components of the ascending arousal system
Because the VLPO neurons synthesize GABA and galanin, their descending projections are likely to be inhibitory.
Thus a reciprocal inhibitory interaction likely exists between the sleep-promoting VLPO and the monoaminergic wake-promoting centres in the caudal hypothalamus and brain stem.
When VLPO neurons fire rapidly during sleep, they would inhibit the monoaminergic cell groups, thus disinhibiting and reinforcing their own firing.
Similarly, when monoamine neurons fire at a high rate during wakefulness, they would inhibit the VLPO, thereby disinhibiting their own firing
However, at onset of REM sleep, noradrenergic and serotoninergic neurons are inhibited by a local GABAergic element, which leads to disinhibition of the cholinergic neurons.

The magnocellular nuclei of the anterior hypothalamus, i.e. the supraoptic and (magnocellular) paraventricular nuclei, give rise to axons that descend through the infundibular stalk to the posterior lobe of the pituitary.

These axons, which together form the supraoptico-paraventriculo-hypophyseal tract, transport colloid droplets containing the hormones oxytocin and vasopressin to the posterior pituitary lobe or neurohypophysis, where they are released into the blood.

In rats, CRH-producing cells are located in a distinct subnucleus of the PVH, but in humans they are scattered throughout the nucleus
Most of the CRH-producing neurons in the PVH project to the neurohemal contact zone in the median eminence (ME).

The cells of the infundibular nucleus are involved in controlling secretion of the anterior pituitary hormones by regulating hormones that stimulate or inhibit the liberation of hormones produced in the pituitary.

The traditional view of co-ordinated reflex micturition holds that micturition is mediated by a spinal cord-brain stem-spinal cord reflex loop, initiated by input from pelvic nerve afferents signaling bladder distension

The reflex loop is closed by an ascending pathway from spinal neurons located within the terminal plexus of pelvic and pudendal nerve afferents in sacral lamina I that terminates in the periaqueductal grey
and a projection of the periaqueductal grey to the pontine micturition region
The pontine micturition region (M-region of Holstege, Barrington’s nucleus [17]) is located in the dorsolateral pontine tegmentum.
It projects bilaterally to the sacral intermediolateral nucleus and the commissural nucleus, which contains the interneurons inhibiting Onuf’s nucleus
The detrusor muscle is innervated by an intra- and juxtamural cholinergic plexus, which is postganglionic to parasympathetic preganglionic fibres from the sacral intermediolateral nucleus
Stimulation of the pontine micturition region results in micturition.
The presence of a pontine micturition region has been confirmed in PET-studies carried out by Blok et al.
